questions.question: Amazon LP: 'Customer Obsession'. What does it mean, and which of your stories fits?
questions.answer: Start with the customer and work backward; earn and keep customer trust. → Name your story (see the mapping table in amazon-leadership-principles.md).

questions.question: Amazon LP: 'Ownership'. What does it mean, and which of your stories fits?
questions.answer: Think long term, act on behalf of the whole company, never say 'that's not my job'. → Name your story (see the mapping table in amazon-leadership-principles.md).

questions.question: Amazon LP: 'Invent and Simplify'. What does it mean, and which of your stories fits?
questions.answer: Expect and require innovation; find ways to simplify; accept ideas from anywhere. → Name your story (see the mapping table in amazon-leadership-principles.md).

questions.question: Amazon LP: 'Are Right, A Lot'. What does it mean, and which of your stories fits?
questions.answer: Strong judgment and instincts; seek diverse perspectives; work to disconfirm your own beliefs. → Name your story (see the mapping table in amazon-leadership-principles.md).

questions.question: Amazon LP: 'Learn and Be Curious'. What does it mean, and which of your stories fits?
questions.answer: Never done learning; explore new possibilities. → Name your story (see the mapping table in amazon-leadership-principles.md).

questions.question: Amazon LP: 'Hire and Develop the Best'. What does it mean, and which of your stories fits?
questions.answer: Raise the performance bar with every hire and promotion; coach others. → Name your story (see the mapping table in amazon-leadership-principles.md).

questions.question: Amazon LP: 'Insist on the Highest Standards'. What does it mean, and which of your stories fits?
questions.answer: Relentlessly high standards; fix problems so they stay fixed. → Name your story (see the mapping table in amazon-leadership-principles.md).

questions.question: Amazon LP: 'Think Big'. What does it mean, and which of your stories fits?
questions.answer: Create and communicate a bold direction that inspires results. → Name your story (see the mapping table in amazon-leadership-principles.md).

questions.question: Amazon LP: 'Bias for Action'. What does it mean, and which of your stories fits?
questions.answer: Speed matters; many decisions are reversible; take calculated risks. → Name your story (see the mapping table in amazon-leadership-principles.md).

questions.question: Amazon LP: 'Frugality'. What does it mean, and which of your stories fits?
questions.answer: Accomplish more with less; no extra points for headcount or budget. → Name your story (see the mapping table in amazon-leadership-principles.md).

questions.question: Amazon LP: 'Earn Trust'. What does it mean, and which of your stories fits?
questions.answer: Listen attentively, speak candidly, be self-critical, benchmark against the best. → Name your story (see the mapping table in amazon-leadership-principles.md).

questions.question: Amazon LP: 'Dive Deep'. What does it mean, and which of your stories fits?
questions.answer: Operate at all levels, stay connected to details, audit frequently, be skeptical when metrics and anecdotes differ. → Name your story (see the mapping table in amazon-leadership-principles.md).

questions.question: Amazon LP: 'Have Backbone; Disagree and Commit'. What does it mean, and which of your stories fits?
questions.answer: Respectfully challenge decisions you disagree with; once decided, commit wholly. → Name your story (see the mapping table in amazon-leadership-principles.md).

questions.question: Amazon LP: 'Deliver Results'. What does it mean, and which of your stories fits?
questions.answer: Focus on key inputs; deliver with quality and on time despite setbacks. → Name your story (see the mapping table in amazon-leadership-principles.md).

questions.question: Amazon LP: 'Strive to be Earth's Best Employer'. What does it mean, and which of your stories fits?
questions.answer: Create a safer, more productive, diverse, and just work environment; lead with empathy. → Name your story (see the mapping table in amazon-leadership-principles.md).

questions.question: Amazon LP: 'Success and Scale Bring Broad Responsibility'. What does it mean, and which of your stories fits?
questions.answer: Be humble and thoughtful about secondary effects; leave things better than you found them. → Name your story (see the mapping table in amazon-leadership-principles.md).

questions.question: How many Amazon Leadership Principles are there today?
questions.explanation: Two were added in 2021: Strive to be Earth's Best Employer, and Success and Scale Bring Broad Responsibility.

questions.question: What is Amazon's 'Bar Raiser'?
options: An experienced interviewer from outside the hiring team who ensures hires raise the bar and can veto
questions.explanation: Expect deeper follow-ups and probing of your weakest-looking area.

questions.question: In STAR-L, roughly what share of a story should be Actions?
questions.explanation: Situation and task are short context; actions show what *you* did; results and learning close it.

questions.question: Which story trait most clearly signals Staff level?
options: Aligning multiple teams on a direction you defined under ambiguity, with measurable business impact
Working long hours to hit a deadline
Fixing a bug quickly on your own
questions.explanation: Scope, ambiguity, influence without authority, and impact.

questions.question: Google's L6 loop typically includes which non-coding rounds?
options: System design (often 2), Role-Related Knowledge, and Googleyness & Leadership
questions.explanation: Followed by hiring committee and team matching.

questions.question: Google's standard coding interview environment usually:
options: Has a full IDE with debugger
Doesn't run code and has no autocomplete, so practice writing correct code without executing it
questions.explanation: Dry-run by hand. (Verify the current format with your recruiter.)

questions.question: Meta's AI-assisted coding round evaluates you mainly on:
options: Problem solving, code quality, how you steer and verify the AI, and communication
How fast the AI can solve the problem alone
questions.explanation: Explain the approach before prompting, delegate small pieces, review every line, and test.

questions.question: Amazon's stated guidance on GenAI tools during interviews (reported 2025):
options: Don't use them unless explicitly permitted; doing so may disqualify you
questions.explanation: Prepare to code unassisted for Amazon.

questions.question: In a Meta loop, the behavioral round:
options: Can change your level (e.g. E5 → E4) on its own

questions.question: What are the 5 parts of STAR-L, with time shares?
questions.answer: Situation (10%) → Task (10%) → Actions (50%, 'I' not 'we') → Result (20%, with numbers) → Learning (10%).

questions.question: What must a good failure story include?
questions.answer: A real failure you owned with real consequences → your part in it → how you limited the damage → the systemic change so it can't recur → what you changed about how you work.

questions.question: Five phrases that signal Staff thinking in a design round.
questions.answer: 'What does success look like in 6 months, and what won't we support?' / 'Two viable options; here's the trade-off and what would make me switch.' / 'The riskiest part is X, so I'd de-risk it first.' / 'This needs agreement from teams A and B; here's how.' / 'I'd measure ..., and roll back if ...'

questions.question: Your top differentiator for applied AI design rounds?
questions.answer: Production depth others lack: evaluation harnesses and release gates, permission-aware retrieval, cost/latency engineering, guardrails, and rollout, backed by real systems you led (an enterprise RAG platform for thousands of users; a ~70K docs/month multi-agent pipeline; teams of 8–20).

questions.question: Workflow for the AI-assisted coding round?
questions.answer: Clarify with the interviewer → design and complexity out loud → delegate small, specific pieces to the AI → review every line and explain it → write/ask for tests, run, fix → revisit the design when a new requirement arrives.

questions.question: Netflix culture: name 3 ideas you should be ready to discuss.
questions.answer: Freedom and responsibility; candid feedback; the 'keeper test' (would your manager fight to keep you?); context, not control; highly aligned, loosely coupled teams.
